provenance.pins: datasheet p.3 PIN table (MSOP-10); thermal pad is DFN-only

designVerdict: SELECTED - hot-swap controller, one per channel (U10, U11). Replaces four failed discrete gate networks.
notes: Tokmas second-source LM5069MMX-2, not TI silicon. Live stock 105 at selection, where jlcsearch claimed 2952 - the staleness the workflow warns about. This is the -2 suffix, which AUTO-RESTARTS (p.13). TI's LM5069MM-1/NOPB (C486026, 89 units, $5.90) is the LATCH-OFF variant. An early note here had the two suffixes backwards.

VIN absolute 108 V, operating 8-90 V (p.1, p.5). Below 8 V it holds the gate down, so the channels are off through the whole 5 V pre-negotiation phase with no firmware involvement. Quote 8 V, not the p.1 headline's 9 V, when the argument rests on the minimum.
Drives an N-channel FET with a charge pump holding GATE ~12 V above OUT (p.3 pin 10). This is what removes the high-side P-FET gate problem entirely: no level shifters, no Vgs clamp Zeners.

DESIGN VALUES, per channel: R_SENSE 10 mOhm, R_PWR 64.9 kOhm (P_LIM 39.8 W via Eq. 14), C_TIMER 6.8 uF, UVLO/OVLO string 82.5k/44.2k/7.50k. Ramp 61 ms typ, 96 ms at the corners. An earlier set (12 mOhm / 32.4 kOhm / 10 uF / 120k-5.11k-7.68k, P_LIM 18 W) is SUPERSEDED and must not be reinstated.

THE TIMER PIN HAS TWO JOBS. p.3 pin 6 sets the insertion time delay as well as the fault timeout, and p.13 holds GATE down through the insertion time 'regardless of the voltage at VIN or UVLO'. The ratio is fixed at 17.5:1 by the datasheet currents (4 uA insertion, 70 uA fault), so 6.8 uF means a 6.1 s typical hold-off at power-on (2.9-13.6 s over the spread, derating the capacitor at the fast end as the fault-timeout calculation already does). Sizing C_TIMER from the fault timeout alone silently buys a multi-second delay.

UVLO doubles as ENABLE: below 2.5 V the channel is off. A 2N7002 drain on UVLO with a 100 kOhm gate pull-up to 3V3 gives fail-safe-off through MCU reset, and firmware drives the GPIO LOW to enable. The FAULT interlock acts on the same node without contending with a driven GPIO - but it needs ONE TRANSISTOR PER CHANNEL, since a single drain tied to both UVLO pins would short the two dividers together.

THRESHOLDS: UVLO rising 7.97 V typ (6.75-9.23 V), OVLO rising 44.7 V typ (39.51-50.15 V), OVLO falling 42.5 V - these DO carry the 1% resistor tolerance as well as the comparator and hysteresis spreads. OVLO margin over the 37.8 V maximum bus is 1.71 V. UVLO is sized for GRACEFUL DEGRADATION - every PDO from 12 V up drives the LEDs - not for the 36 V contract. An earlier 28 V setting made the output work at 36 V and nowhere else. Margins must carry the 1% resistor tolerance, not just the +/-10% comparator spread - on the first divider the stated 1.1 V of OVLO margin was really 0.4 V.

OVLO at 44.7 V nominal trips ABOVE the SMAJ36CA's 40.0-44.2 V breakdown, so on a sustained overvoltage the TVS conducts first. OVLO could not protect it anyway: it sheds the channels, and the TVS sits upstream of the switches.

The current limit (4.8-6.5 A per channel at 10 mOhm) cannot sit both above the 4.0 A white-flash peak and below the 5.0 A PD contract. On a hard short the source's protection acts first, so per-channel autonomous isolation is NOT reliably obtainable.

AUTO-RESTART PERIOD is ~64 s with C_TIMER 6.8 uF: seven complete cycles (2.8 V discharge at 2.5 uA plus recharge at 70 uA) plus the eighth ramp to 0.3 V. Counting only the seven discharges gives ~53 s and is wrong; the datasheet's 0.5% fault duty cycle corroborates 64 s.

MSOP-10 RthJA is 156 C/W (p.1), which sounds alarming and is not: IQ is 650 uA max at 37.8 V, about 25 mW. The MSOP-10 part has NO exposed pad - the pad in the package drawings belongs to the DFN3x3 variant - so GND (pin 5) is the only ground connection.

WHY THE LOW UVLO IS SAFE: the 28 V setting did not shed cleanly anyway - with hysteresis from 26.2 to 28.3 V a source sagging into that band oscillates, re-ramping every 61 ms. What protects a brownout is unchanged: the current limit stays active at 5.5 A per channel however far the bus falls, FAULT sheds both channels when the source reports it cannot supply, and the software limiter scales to the contract. t_start also improves at lower voltages (ratio 1.9x at 36 V, 5.8x at 20 V, 14x at 12 V), so the module ceiling relaxes with the contract.

THE LOWERED UVLO MADE THE FAULT INTERLOCK 3.9x HARDER. With the 82.5k string the UVLO node sits at 3.61 V behind a stiffer divider, so pulling it below 2.5 V needs 380 uA where the old 120k string needed 97 uA - more than the current at which the 2N7002's 2.5 V threshold is itself specified.
